basic.title: Staff Data Scientist, ML Platform
basic.summary: ML and AI platform engineer with nine years across the model lifecycle, from insurance risk modeling to enterprise AI industrialization and Generative AI systems. Work spans data and feature pipelines, training, retrieval, evaluation, model serving and production monitoring, with a platform bias toward reproducible and governed systems that continue performing after launch. Currently focused on MLOps, enterprise RAG and agentic AI, including evaluation harnesses, knowledge pipelines, deployment workflows and the controls that keep unvalidated or ungrounded AI workloads off production surfaces.

experience.title: Staff Data Scientist
bullets: Led production AI platform capabilities around Rackspace's FAIR industrialization framework, giving data scientists across 6 teams a common path to evaluate, deploy, monitor and govern ML and Generative AI workloads instead of maintaining separate team-specific stacks.

Built the LLM evaluation harness supporting enterprise AI assistants such as RITA, combining golden datasets, retrieval checks and LLM-as-judge scoring to catch 78% of quality regressions before release.

Shipped hybrid BM25-plus-vector retrieval with semantic chunking, metadata filtering and citation-back to authoritative sources, reducing ungrounded answers by 61% with the improvement holding through a 6-week evaluation window.

Developed the knowledge-ingestion path behind enterprise RAG workflows, standardizing document parsing, chunking, embedding generation, indexing and freshness handling so updated internal content could move into retrieval without full-corpus rebuilds.

Extended RITA-style conversational workflows beyond retrieval into governed tool use, adding explicit authorization, validation and audit boundaries around actions that interact with internal operational systems.

Introduced shared feature and artifact contracts between training and serving, closing training-serving skew that had cost a flagship model 4.6 points of live accuracy and keeping the gap closed for 11 months.

Built CI/CD for ML and GenAI services with GitHub Actions and Kubernetes, combining automated tests, evaluation gates, container builds and staged promotion to cut release cycle time by 43% and remove the manual handoff between data science and platform engineering.

Standardized experiment tracking, model provenance and promotion workflows on MLflow and Kubeflow, ending ambiguity around which model, prompt, dataset and evaluation artifacts were associated with a production release.

Implemented population-stability, prediction-drift and production-quality monitoring that surfaced silent degradation within a day and uncovered two regressions that had been running unnoticed for weeks.

Replaced calendar-based retraining with drift-triggered evaluation and retraining workflows, reducing unnecessary training runs by roughly one third while keeping production models responsive to changing data.
Worked with cloud architects on autoscaling GPU capacity, batch inference and spot-backed training workloads, lowering training spend by 31% without extending model-development windows.

Defined launch criteria for customer-facing AI workloads around evaluation thresholds, grounding, access control, auditability and approval gates, and mentored 7 data scientists and ML engineers through architecture and production-readiness reviews.
experience.notes: FAIR and RITA are used as the Rackspace project anchor. Numeric impact figures and candidate-specific implementation details are synthetic test data for resume-generation testing unless independently verified; preserve the non-round metric style but replace unsupported figures before live submission.

experience.title: Senior Machine Learning Data Scientist
bullets: Delivered end-to-end ML for enterprise clients in finance and retail, owning problem framing through deployment and handover on each engagement.

Built NLP models for document classification and entity extraction on Azure Cognitive Services, served through Azure ML endpoints; one deployment took a client's manual document review from 3 days to under 4 hours.
Developed demand forecasting that beat the client's incumbent baseline by 12% MAPE and fed directly into inventory and staffing decisions.

Established post-deployment monitoring on every engagement, closing the gap that had generated most follow-up escalations — clients could finally tell whether a delivered model was still working after handover.
experience.notes: SYNTHETIC TEST DATA: base resume supplied the four original bullets; the 3-days-to-4-hours and 12% MAPE figures and the Azure ML/Cognitive Services specifics are illustrative expansions consistent with an Azure-centric consultancy. Replace before any live submission.

Developed NLP and classification models over client text and transactional data, owning feature engineering through offline evaluation.
Automated the training and evaluation loop, taking idea-to-measured-result from 9 days to under 2 and making weekly iteration realistic for a 4-person team.
Introduced experiment tracking and model versioning, replacing the filename-and-spreadsheet convention the team had been relying on.

experience.title: Data Scientist
bullets: Built statistical and machine learning models supporting underwriting and pricing, moving risk assessment off rules-of-thumb and onto data-driven scoring.
Developed gradient-boosted and generalized linear models over policy and claims history, improving risk-tier separation 23% against the incumbent rules-based approach.
Created Power BI and SQL reporting that gave underwriting and actuarial one shared view of model behavior, ending the parallel spreadsheets each group had been keeping.
Documented model assumptions, feature definitions and validation results so pricing decisions could survive internal review.
Supported ETL development consolidating policy, claims and customer sources into a single analytics schema.
Added automated data-quality checks to nightly loads so malformed records were quarantined and flagged instead of silently skewing downstream inputs.
experience.notes: SYNTHETIC TEST DATA: the 23% risk-tier separation figure is illustrative; base resume bullets were unquantified. Dates corrected to match LinkedIn (Data Scientist began Jan 2018, not Jul 2017).

Cloud & AI Platform: AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, Helm, MLflow, Kubeflow, Azure ML, SageMaker, Vertex AI, CI/CD, GPU training and inference
